review_notes: I read the whole file and the sources it uses. I checked the BoundaryFunctional block (extendDriver, solution, solutionPath, position, variation, logDerivative) against Mathlib's Set.IccExtend, Set.projIcc and ContinuousMap.IccExtend. I also checked the near-identical definitions in StoppedIto.lean. The BoundaryCutoff wrappers (clampRe, velocity) are named specialisations, and so are the Cutoff structure and shrinkingAngle, so I did not flag them. The radial and lyapunov definitions, and derivWithin_left/right, are not parallel Mathlib concepts or are theorem-level, so they are excluded. The finding is moderate. The cost is small repeated glue, and extendDriver includes a rescaling t/T. I did not check whether Mathlib has a continuity lemma specific to Set.IccExtend. I only point to the ContinuousMap.IccExtend bundled version, which exists.

findings.excerpt: solutionPath hε hT U z (projIcc 0 T hT t)
findings.problem: `position` is the clamp-and-extend of the path `solutionPath : C(Icc 0 T, ℂ)` to all of ℝ. That is exactly Mathlib's `Set.IccExtend hT (solutionPath ..)`, which is defined as `f ∘ projIcc a b h`. `extendDriver T U` is likewise `IccExtend zero_le_one U` composed with `(· / T)`. Because the file builds these by hand with raw `projIcc`, it has to reprove facts Mathlib already has. `position_eq` unfolds `projIcc` and uses `max_eq_right`/`min_eq_right`, where `IccExtend_of_mem` states it directly. The `continuous_projIcc.comp ...` plumbing in `continuous_extendDriver`, `continuous_position` and `continuous_joint_extendDriver` is repeated by hand. The same `extendDriver` definition is also written out a second time in StoppedIto.lean, in the `LoewnerCutoff` namespace.
findings.proposed_change: Define `position hε hT U z := Set.IccExtend hT (solutionPath hε hT U z)`. Define `extendDriver T U t := Set.IccExtend zero_le_one U (t / T)`. Keep the names `position` and `extendDriver` as the public API. Prove `position_eq` from `Set.IccExtend_of_mem`. Where a bundled continuous map is wanted, use `ContinuousMap.IccExtend`. Ideally also share one `extendDriver` between the LoewnerCutoff and BoundaryFunctional namespaces.
findings.benefit: The Mathlib `IccExtend` lemma API (`IccExtend_of_mem`, `IccExtend_left`, `IccExtend_range`, and so on) works on these objects directly, so there are fewer ad-hoc `projIcc` unfoldings. The extension-by-clamping convention is the standard one and stays visible to readers. The duplicated definition across namespaces is removed.

evidence.excerpt:
def IccExtend {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) (f : Icc a b → β) : α → β :=
  f ∘ projIcc a b h
theorem IccExtend_of_mem (f : Icc a b → β) (hx : x ∈ Icc a b) : IccExtend h f x = f ⟨x, hx⟩

def IccExtend (f : C(Set.Icc a b, β)) : C(α, β) where
  toFun := Set.IccExtend h f

def extendDriver (T : ℝ) (U : C(I, ℝ)) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  U (projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one (t / T))
